title: Massage for rehabilitation after total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

items.ai_reason: Title explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Background places the review in context of KOA/TKA complications, conflicting prior RCTs, and absence of previous systematic reviews.
Objectives are stated explicitly as assessing massage effects on post-TKA rehabilitation via systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs.
PICOS-based inclusion/exclusion criteria are specified; studies grouped by outcomes, time points, and country for syntheses.
All databases searched (PubMed, Web of Science, EMBASE, Cochrane, CNKI) and last search date (May 2024) are specified.
Full search strategies, including strings and limits, are presented in Supplementary Table S1.
Two reviewers independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts; disagreements resolved by discussion or third party; EndNote used.
Two researchers independently extracted data; disagreements resolved by discussion or third party; no investigator contact reported.
Outcomes (pain, ROM, D-dimer, length of stay) listed but not defined; no statement on seeking all compatible results or selection methods.
Extracted variables listed but not defined; no description of assumptions about missing or unclear information.
Cochrane RoB tool named, but number of reviewers, independence, and any automation for assessments not specified.
MD or SMD with 95% CI specified for all continuous outcomes used in syntheses.
No description of processes (e.g., tabulating characteristics versus planned groups) to decide study eligibility for each synthesis.
No methods described for preparing data, handling missing summary statistics, or performing conversions.
Methods used to tabulate or visually display results (tables, forest plots) not described in the methods section.
Meta-analysis methods, fixed/random models based on I2, heterogeneity statistics (Q, I2), and software (RevMan, Stata) described with rationale.
Subgroup analyses by country type described to explore heterogeneity sources.
No methods for sensitivity analyses described in methods (only noted as not performed due to few studies).
Publication bias (reporting bias) assessed using Begg’s and Egger’s tests.
No methods (e.g., GRADE) described for assessing certainty in the body of evidence.
Search and selection results from 554 records to 11 included studies described, with flow diagram (Fig. 1).
Reasons for excluding 10 full-text articles given by category, but the studies themselves are not cited.
All 11 included studies are cited and their characteristics presented in Table 1.
Risk-of-bias assessments for included studies presented in text and Fig. 2.
Forest plots present per-study summary statistics, effect estimates, and precision for all outcomes.
No brief summary of characteristics and risk of bias among studies contributing to each individual synthesis.
Meta-analysis summary estimates, CIs, p-values, I2, and effect directions presented for each synthesis.
Subgroup analysis results exploring heterogeneity (country) for length of stay are presented.
No sensitivity analyses were conducted, so no results presented.
Publication-bias assessments via Egger/Begg tests presented for syntheses with enough studies.
No assessments of certainty in the body of evidence presented for any outcome.
Results interpreted in context of pain/ROM mechanisms, prior knowledge, and other rehabilitation methods.
Limitations of included evidence discussed (China-centric studies, blinding issues, quality, heterogeneity).
Limitations of review processes discussed (possible missed grey literature, no sensitivity analyses).
Implications for practice (adjunctive use) and future research (standardization, higher-quality trials) discussed.
PROSPERO registration name and number (CRD42023411680) provided.
Protocol access indicated via PROSPERO registration number.
No description or explanation of any protocol/registration amendments (or statement that none occurred).
Funding reported as not applicable, implying no sources or funder roles.
Authors declare they have no competing interests.
Only datasets available on request from author; no report on public availability of forms, extracted data, code, or other materials.
The title explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review and meta-analysis.
The abstract states the aim to evaluate the effectiveness of massage for postoperative rehabilitation after TKA.
Only inclusion of RCTs of massage after TKA is stated; exclusion criteria are not specified.
Five databases are named and the search period is given as from inception to May 2024.
The Cochrane Risk of Bias Assessment Tool is named as the method used.
A meta-analysis of named outcomes is specified as the synthesis method.
Eleven trials and 940 participants are given, but relevant study characteristics are not summarised.
Effect directions are described, but no summary estimates or confidence intervals are reported despite meta-analysis.
Large heterogeneity of the included studies is noted as a limitation.
Results are interpreted and massage is recommended as adjunctive post-TKA rehabilitation.
No funding source for the review is specified.
No register name or registration number is provided.

Mean difference specified as the effect measure for pain scores and GPE in the syntheses.

No methods described for handling missing summary statistics or performing data conversions.
